speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the history of repetitive pivoting in volleyball and the recent onset of worsening pain, is the pain localized specifically to the inner (medial) side of your knee or the front? Also, does the knee feel unstable or "give way" when you try to pivot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain is located on the medial aspect of the tibia, just below the kneecap. Given the history of repetitive pivoting in volleyball and recent increased activity, this sounds like a tibial sesamoid fracture or a medial plica syndrome; does the area feel tender to the touch, and can you bear weight on the leg?
